common_collocations: wash your hands in the basin

meanings.explanation: A [basin] is a round, bowl-shaped container that holds water, like a sink in a bathroom.

examples.english: Mom filled the [basin] with warm water.
examples.chinese: 妈妈在[盆]里倒满了温水。

examples.english: I wash my face in the [basin] every morning.
examples.chinese: 我每天早上都在[脸盆]里洗脸。

examples.english: The cat drank water from the [basin].
examples.chinese: 小猫从[盆]里喝水。

meanings.explanation: An [attraction] is a fun or interesting place that people like to go and see.

examples.english: The ferris wheel is the most popular [attraction] in the park.
examples.chinese: 摩天轮是公园里最受欢迎的[景点]。

examples.english: The zoo is a great [attraction] for kids.
examples.chinese: 动物园对孩子们来说是个很棒的[景点]。

examples.english: There are many [attractions] to visit in Beijing.
examples.chinese: 北京有很多值得参观的[景点]。

common_collocations: be used to getting up early

meanings.explanation: If you [be used to] something, it feels normal or easy for you because you have done it a lot.

examples.english: I [am used to] eating rice every day.
examples.chinese: 我[习惯]每天吃米饭。

examples.english: She [is used to] waking up early.
examples.chinese: 她[习惯]早起。

examples.english: They [are used to] the cold weather here.
examples.chinese: 他们[习惯]了这里的寒冷天气。

meanings.explanation: If someone or something [appears to] do something, they seem to do it or seem to have a particular quality.

examples.english: The puppy [appears to] be hungry.
examples.chinese: 这只小狗[好像]饿了。

examples.english: Lucy [appeared to] know the answer.
examples.chinese: 露西[似乎]知道答案。

examples.english: The sky [appears to] be getting darker.
examples.chinese: 天[看起来]越来越暗了。

derived_forms: at a first glance (similar variant expression)
common_collocations: at a first look it seems
at a first look it appears
at a first look it looks

meanings.explanation: When you judge or see something [at a first look], you form a quick initial opinion about it before you look at it more carefully.

examples.english: [At a first look], this toy car looks broken.
examples.chinese: [乍一看]，这个玩具车像是坏了。

examples.english: This cake looks very big [at a first look], but it's actually small.
examples.chinese: 这个蛋糕[乍一看]很大，但实际上很小。

examples.english: [At a first look], this math problem looks really hard.
examples.chinese: [乍一看]，这道数学题看起来很难。

common_collocations: compare your answer against the key

meanings.explanation: If you [compare one thing against another], you look at them together to see how they are similar or different.

examples.english: I [compare my old shoes against my new ones] to see which pair is bigger.
examples.chinese: 我把[旧鞋和新鞋放在一起比较]，看看哪双更大。

examples.english: Please [compare your answer against the key] to check your homework.
examples.chinese: 请把你的答案和答案册[进行比较]，检查一下作业。

examples.english: Mom [compared the two apples against each other] to find the sweetest one.
examples.chinese: 妈妈把[两个苹果放在一起比较]，找出最甜的那个。

meanings.explanation: If something is [deadly], it is very dangerous and can cause death.

examples.english: Some wild mushrooms are [deadly], so we should never eat them.
examples.chinese: 有些野生蘑菇是[致命的]，所以我们千万不能吃。

examples.english: The zookeeper told us that this snake's bite is [deadly].
examples.chinese: 饲养员告诉我们，这种蛇的咬伤是[致命的]。

examples.english: That [deadly] poison must be kept away from children.
examples.chinese: 那种[致命的]毒药要放在孩子够不到的地方。

meanings.explanation: A [creature] is any living thing, especially an animal that is not a person.

examples.english: A little [creature] crawled out from under the rock.
examples.chinese: 一只小[生物]从石头下面爬了出来。

examples.english: Butterflies are the most beautiful [creatures] in the garden.
examples.chinese: 蝴蝶是花园里最美的[动物]。

examples.english: The zookeeper takes good care of every [creature] in the zoo.
examples.chinese: 动物园管理员细心照顾园里的每一只[动物]。

meanings.explanation: If something happens [at times], it happens sometimes, but not all the time.

examples.english: [At times] I feel a little scared of the dark.
examples.chinese: 我[有时]会有点怕黑。

examples.english: My little brother is really noisy [at times], but I still love him.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟[有时候]很吵，但我还是很爱他。

examples.english: In winter, it can get very cold here [at times].
examples.chinese: 冬天的时候，这里[有时]会非常冷。

meanings.explanation: If you [are worried about] something, you feel uneasy or scared because you think something bad may happen.

examples.english: I [am worried about] tomorrow's math test.
examples.chinese: 我[担心]明天的数学考试。

examples.english: Mom [is worried about] the heavy rain.
examples.chinese: 妈妈[担心]下大雨。

examples.english: She [was worried about] her little dog getting lost.
examples.chinese: 她[担心]小狗走丢了。

meanings.explanation: If you [are ready for] something, you have prepared for it and can deal with it.

examples.english: I [am ready for] school.
examples.chinese: 我[准备好上学]了。

examples.english: You [are ready for] the rain because you have your umbrella.
examples.chinese: 你带了雨伞，已经[做好下雨的准备]了。

examples.english: Mia [was ready for] the birthday party.
examples.chinese: 米娅[准备好参加生日派对]了。

meanings.explanation: If one thing [be related to] another thing, the two things are connected to each other in some way.

examples.english: My bad stomachache [is related to] eating too many candies.
examples.chinese: 我肚子痛得厉害，这和吃太多糖果[有关]。

examples.english: Today's art lesson [is related to] drawing cute cats.
examples.chinese: 今天的美术课和画可爱的小猫[有关]。

examples.english: This story [is related to] a brave little boy.
examples.chinese: 这个故事和一个勇敢的小男孩[有关]。

meanings.explanation: A [deserted] place has no people in it because everyone has left.

examples.english: The playground was [deserted] after dark.
examples.chinese: 天黑后，操场上[空无一人]。

examples.english: We walked along a [deserted] street on Sunday morning.
examples.chinese: 星期天早上，我们走在一条[空荡荡的]街上。

examples.english: The old house looked [deserted] and dusty.
examples.chinese: 那座老房子看起来[荒废了]，到处都是灰尘。

meanings.explanation: You use [consequently] to show that something happens as a result of the thing you have just mentioned.

examples.english: It rained very hard yesterday, [consequently] we couldn't go to the park.
examples.chinese: 昨天雨下得特别大，[因此]我们没能去公园。

examples.english: Lily studied very hard for her test, [consequently] she got full marks.
examples.chinese: 莉莉为了考试认真复习，[所以]她拿到了满分。

examples.english: I forgot my lunch money, [consequently] I shared food with my friend.
examples.chinese: 我忘了带午餐钱，[结果]我和朋友分吃了食物。

common_collocations: compare your answer with a classmate's

meanings.explanation: If you [compare one thing with another], you look at both to see how they are alike or different.

examples.english: Please [compare this apple with that one] before you choose.
examples.chinese: 请[把这个苹果和那个苹果比较一下]，再选一个。

examples.english: I [compared my drawing with my sister's] and saw that they were different.
examples.chinese: 我[把我的画和姐姐的画比较了一下]，发现它们不一样。

examples.english: We are [comparing the two schoolbags with each other] to find which one is lighter.
examples.chinese: 我们正在[比较这两个书包]，看看哪个更轻。

synonyms: look at A and B side by side

meanings.explanation: If something is [electric], it works by using electricity.

examples.english: My little brother got an [electric] toy car for his birthday.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟生日时得到了一辆[电动]玩具车。

examples.english: We turn on the [electric] fan when it is hot.
examples.chinese: 天热的时候，我们打开[电]风扇。

examples.english: This [electric] toothbrush cleans my teeth very well.
examples.chinese: 这把[电动]牙刷能把我的牙齿刷得很干净。

meanings.explanation: When people or things are [close against each other], they are positioned very near one another, often touching or pressing gently against each other.

examples.english: The books on the shelf are [close against each other].
examples.chinese: 书架上的书[紧挨着彼此]。

examples.english: We sat [close against each other] to stay warm on the cold day.
examples.chinese: 天冷的时候，我们[紧紧靠在一起]坐着取暖。

examples.english: The baby birds sit [close against each other] in their nest.
examples.chinese: 鸟宝宝们在鸟窝里[紧紧挨在一起]。

meanings.explanation: The [edge] of something is the border where it ends, like the side of a table or the sharp side of a knife.

examples.english: The cat is sitting on the [edge] of the bed.
examples.chinese: 小猫坐在床[边]。

examples.english: Don't put your cup on the [edge] of the table.
examples.chinese: 别把杯子放在桌子[边]上。

examples.english: This knife has a very sharp [edge].
examples.chinese: 这把刀的[刀刃]很锋利。

meanings.explanation: If you [dream about] someone or something, you see pictures and stories about them in your mind while you are asleep.

examples.english: Last night, I [dreamed about] a big friendly dinosaur.
examples.chinese: 昨天晚上，我[梦到]了一只又大又友好的恐龙。

examples.english: She often [dreams about] playing with her pet cat.
examples.chinese: 她经常[梦见]和她的宠物猫一起玩。

examples.english: Did you [dream about] anything fun last night?
examples.chinese: 你昨天晚上有没有[梦到]什么有趣的事？

meanings.explanation: If an accident or illness is [fatal], it causes death or is so serious that someone dies from it.

examples.english: The doctor said the disease was [fatal].
examples.chinese: 医生说这种病是[致命的]。

examples.english: Crossing the road carelessly can be [fatal].
examples.chinese: 过马路不小心可能是[致命的]。

examples.english: The snake's poison is [fatal] to small animals.
examples.chinese: 蛇的毒液对小动物来说是[致命的]。

meanings.explanation: If a person or place is [famous], many people know about them.

examples.english: My teacher is [famous] for singing funny songs.
examples.chinese: 我的老师因为唱有趣的歌而[出名]。

examples.english: This city is [famous] for its delicious food.
examples.chinese: 这座城市以美食[闻名]。

examples.english: Pandas are [famous] animals from China.
examples.chinese: 熊猫是来自中国的[著名]动物。

meanings.explanation: If something [exceeds] a number or amount, it is greater or more than that number.

examples.english: The number of students in our class [exceeds] thirty.
examples.chinese: 我们班的学生人数[超过]了三十人。

examples.english: Her test score [exceeded] everyone's expectations.
examples.chinese: 她的考试成绩[超过]了所有人的期望。

examples.english: The box [exceeds] the weight limit, so it needs a bigger stamp.
examples.chinese: 这个盒子[超过]了重量限制，所以需要更大的邮票。

meanings.explanation: If you [deal with] a problem, a task, or a difficult situation, you handle it and take care of it.

examples.english: I have a big problem to [deal with] today.
examples.chinese: 我今天有个大问题要[处理]。

examples.english: My mom [dealt with] the broken chair all by herself.
examples.chinese: 妈妈自己一个人就[处理]好了那把坏椅子。

examples.english: Tom is [dealing with] a lot of homework this week.
examples.chinese: 汤姆这周要[处理]一大堆作业。

meanings.explanation: When you [get energy from] something, that thing gives you power to move, play, and stay active.

examples.english: I [get energy from] eating a good breakfast.
examples.chinese: 我吃一顿丰盛的早餐就能[获得能量]。

examples.english: Plants [get energy from] the sun.
examples.chinese: 植物[从太阳那里获得能量]。

examples.english: She [got energy from] a long nap.
examples.chinese: 她睡了个长长的午觉，[恢复了精力]。

meanings.explanation: If you [embarrass] someone, you make them feel awkward or ashamed, especially in front of other people.

examples.english: My little brother [embarrassed] me by calling me “Mom” at school.
examples.chinese: 弟弟在学校叫我“妈妈”，让我觉得很[尴尬]。

examples.english: The funny picture [embarrassed] Mia when her classmates saw it.
examples.chinese: 同学们看到那张搞笑的照片时，米娅觉得很[难为情]。

examples.english: I did not mean to [embarrass] Dad with my silly joke.
examples.chinese: 我讲那个傻傻的笑话，不是想让爸爸觉得[尴尬]。

meanings.explanation: If something [is caused by] something else, the second thing makes the first thing happen.

examples.english: The broken window [was caused by] the strong wind.
examples.chinese: 窗户破了是大风[造成的]。

examples.english: The flood [was caused by] the heavy rain.
examples.chinese: 洪水是暴雨[造成的]。

examples.english: The loud noise [is caused by] the passing train.
examples.chinese: 这么大的响声是路过的火车[造成的]。

meanings.explanation: An [illusion] is something that looks real but is not really true; it tricks your eyes or your mind.

examples.english: The magician's trick was just an [illusion].
examples.chinese: 魔术师的把戏只是一个[错觉]。

examples.english: That drawing is an [illusion]; the lines look bent, but they are straight.
examples.chinese: 那幅画是一个[错觉]，线条看起来是弯的，但其实是直的。

examples.english: The tired traveler saw an [illusion] of water in the desert.
examples.chinese: 那位疲惫的旅行者在沙漠里看到了水的[幻影]。

meanings.explanation: When you [get confused], you cannot think clearly or understand something properly.

examples.english: I [get confused] when there are too many steps in one math problem.
examples.chinese: 一道数学题里步骤太多的话，我就会[糊涂]。

examples.english: My cousin [got confused] when he first tried to tie his shoelaces.
examples.chinese: 我表哥第一次学系鞋带时，一下子就[搞不清]了。

examples.english: Don't [get confused]—the blue cup is yours, not mine.
examples.chinese: 别[弄混]了，蓝色杯子是你的，不是我的。

meanings.explanation: [enzymes] are natural substances from living organisms that help break down food and make other important chemical processes happen.

examples.english: Our bodies have special [enzymes] that help us digest the food we eat.
examples.chinese: 我们的身体里有特殊的[酶]，帮助我们消化吃下的食物。

examples.english: Some [enzymes] in apples help break down sugar to give the apple energy.
examples.chinese: 苹果中的一些[酶]会帮助分解糖分，为苹果提供能量。

examples.english: Yogurt contains helpful [enzymes] that are good for our stomachs.
examples.chinese: 酸奶含有对我们肠胃有益的[酶]。

meanings.explanation: [electrical] means relating to electricity, or using electricity to work.

examples.english: We must not touch [electrical] wires with wet hands.
examples.chinese: 我们不能用湿手碰[电线]。

examples.english: My dad fixed the [electrical] outlet in my room.
examples.chinese: 爸爸把我房间里的[插座]修好了。

examples.english: Don't play with [electrical] appliances.
examples.chinese: 不要玩[电器]。

meanings.explanation: The [future] is the time that will come after the present.

examples.english: I hope to travel around the world in the [future].
examples.chinese: 我希望[将来]能环游世界。

examples.english: We do not know what the [future] will bring.
examples.chinese: 我们不知道[未来]会发生什么。

examples.english: We should make plans for the [future].
examples.chinese: 我们应该为[未来]做好计划。

meanings.explanation: If something is [for now], it is true or happening at this moment, but it may change later.

examples.english: I will stay at home [for now] and play later.
examples.chinese: 我[暂时]待在家里，晚点再玩。

examples.english: We can watch TV [for now], and go out when the rain stops.
examples.chinese: 下雨天我们[暂时]看电视，等雨停了再出去。

examples.english: That's all [for now]. See you tomorrow!
examples.chinese: [暂时]就先到这儿吧，明天见！

meanings.explanation: If you [get to work] on something, you start doing it.

examples.english: It's time to [get to work] on my homework.
examples.chinese: 该开始[动手做]作业了。

examples.english: We [got to work] on our craft project right away.
examples.chinese: 我们马上[动手做]手工了。

examples.english: Let's [get to work] and clean up the toys.
examples.chinese: 我们[开始干活]，把玩具收拾一下吧。

derived_forms: in short, what I mean is ... (summary pattern)

meanings.explanation: When you say [in short], you give the main idea in only a few words.

examples.english: [In short], the movie was funny and exciting.
examples.chinese: [总之]，这部电影既有趣又刺激。

examples.english: [In short], we need to clean our room before dinner.
examples.chinese: [简单地说]，我们得在晚饭前打扫房间。

examples.english: [In short], Mia won the race because she practiced every day.
examples.chinese: [简而言之]，米娅每天练习，所以赢得了比赛。

meanings.explanation: If you [look closely at] something, you look at it very carefully to see small or hidden details.

examples.english: I [look closely at] the picture to find the hidden cat.
examples.chinese: 我[仔细观察]这幅画，想找出藏起来的猫。

examples.english: She [looked closely at] the little bug on the leaf.
examples.chinese: 她[仔细观察]了树叶上的小虫子。

examples.english: Tom [looks closely at] the map before we go.
examples.chinese: 出发前，汤姆会[仔细观察]地图。

meanings.explanation: An [insect] is a tiny animal with six legs and a body in three parts, such as an ant or a butterfly.

examples.english: I found a small [insect] on the leaf.
examples.chinese: 我在叶子上发现了一只小[昆虫]。

examples.english: This [insect] has six legs and two wings.
examples.chinese: 这只[昆虫]有六条腿和两只翅膀。

examples.english: My sister likes to watch [insects] in the garden.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐喜欢在花园里观察[昆虫]。

meanings.explanation: An [image] is a picture of a person or thing, such as one you see in a photo, a mirror, or on a screen.

examples.english: I saw a beautiful [image] of a rainbow on my computer screen.
examples.chinese: 我在电脑屏幕上看到了一张漂亮的彩虹[图片]。

examples.english: This [image] shows my family having a picnic in the park.
examples.chinese: 这张[照片]拍的是我们一家人在公园野餐。

examples.english: Can you find the little cat in this [image]?
examples.chinese: 你能在这幅[图画]里找到那只小猫吗？

meanings.explanation: If something [looks different from] another thing, it does not look the same as it.

examples.english: My new school bag [looks different from] my old one.
examples.chinese: 我的新书包[看起来和旧的那个不同]。

examples.english: This toy car [looks different from] the one in the picture.
examples.chinese: 这辆玩具车[看起来和图片里的那辆不一样]。

examples.english: After the rain, the garden [looked different from] before.
examples.chinese: 下过雨后，花园[看起来和以前不一样了]。

meanings.explanation: If you are [in your pajamas], you are wearing the comfortable loose clothes that you wear for sleeping.

examples.english: When you stay home from school, you can play games [in your pajamas].
examples.chinese: 你不上学待在家里的时候，可以[穿着睡衣]玩游戏。

examples.english: After you take a warm bath, you can read picture books [in your pajamas].
examples.chinese: 洗完热水澡后，你可以[穿着睡衣]看绘本。

examples.english: On lazy Saturday mornings, you can eat breakfast [in your pajamas].
examples.chinese: 慵懒的周六早上，你可以[穿着睡衣]吃早餐。

meanings.explanation: A [movement] is the act of moving your body or a part of your body from one place or position to another.

examples.english: My little sister made a funny [movement] with her arms.
examples.chinese: 我妹妹用手臂做了一个好笑的[动作]。

examples.english: I saw a sudden [movement] in the grass.
examples.chinese: 我看到草丛里突然有[动静]。

examples.english: Don't make any [movement] while I take your photo.
examples.chinese: 我给你拍照的时候，千万不要做任何[动作]。

meanings.explanation: [Nectar] is the sweet liquid inside flowers that bees, butterflies, and birds love to drink.

examples.english: Bees collect [nectar] from flowers to make honey.
examples.chinese: 蜜蜂从花中采集[花蜜]来酿蜜。

examples.english: Hummingbirds love to drink sweet [nectar].
examples.chinese: 蜂鸟喜欢喝甜甜的[花蜜]。

examples.english: The butterfly sipped [nectar] from the red flower.
examples.chinese: 蝴蝶从红花上吸食[花蜜]。

meanings.explanation: Your [mind] is the part of you that you use to think, feel, remember, and understand things.

examples.english: I do puzzles every day to keep my [mind] sharp.
examples.chinese: 我每天玩拼图，让我的[头脑]保持灵活。

examples.english: That fun cartoon song keeps popping into my [mind] in class.
examples.chinese: 那首好听的动画主题曲上课时总出现在我的[脑海]里。

examples.english: You should always tell your mom what's on your [mind].
examples.chinese: 你应该告诉妈妈你[心里]在想什么。

meanings.explanation: A [mistake] is something you do wrongly, like a wrong answer or a small error.

examples.english: I made a [mistake] on my math test.
examples.chinese: 我数学考试时犯了一个[错]。

examples.english: It is okay to make a [mistake] when you learn.
examples.chinese: 学习的时候犯个[错误]没关系。

examples.english: Oops, I made a [mistake] in my drawing.
examples.chinese: 哎呀，我在画里出了一个[错]。

meanings.explanation: You use [not everyone] to say that something is true of some people but not all people.

examples.english: [Not everyone] likes broccoli.
examples.chinese: [不是每个人]都喜欢西兰花。

examples.english: [Not everyone] can swim.
examples.chinese: [不是每个人]都会游泳。

examples.english: [Not everyone] has a pet at home.
examples.chinese: [不是每个人]家里都有宠物。

meanings.explanation: If something happened [only recently], it happened a short time ago, not long before now.

examples.english: My family [only recently] moved to this town.
examples.chinese: 我家[不久前]才搬到这个镇上。

examples.english: I [only recently] learned how to ride a bike.
examples.chinese: 我[最近]才学会骑自行车。

examples.english: Tom [only recently] started taking piano lessons.
examples.chinese: 汤姆[不久前]才开始上钢琴课。

meanings.explanation: When you [notice] something, you become aware of it through seeing, hearing, or feeling it.

examples.english: I [notice] that you have a new backpack today.
examples.chinese: 我[注意到]你今天背了新书包。

examples.english: Mom didn't [notice] I ate a cookie before dinner.
examples.chinese: 妈妈没[发现]我饭前吃了一块饼干。

examples.english: If you look closely, you will [notice] the tiny ant on the flower.
examples.chinese: 仔细看，你就能[发现]花朵上的这只小蚂蚁。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [memorable] is so special, interesting, or enjoyable that people remember it for a long time.

examples.english: My birthday party was [memorable] because all my friends came.
examples.chinese: 我的生日派对令人[难忘]，因为我的朋友们都来了。

examples.english: We had a [memorable] day at the beach.
examples.chinese: 我们在海边度过了[难忘]的一天。

examples.english: The school play was a [memorable] experience for me.
examples.chinese: 对我来说，那场校园演出是一段[难忘]的经历。

meanings.explanation: If something is [optical], it is connected with light, sight, or eyes, especially tools that use light to help us see things clearly.

examples.english: This picture is an [optical] illusion.
examples.chinese: 这幅图画是一个[视觉]错觉。

examples.english: We saw tiny cells through an [optical] microscope.
examples.chinese: 我们用[光学]显微镜看到了微小的细胞。

examples.english: The school has an [optical] telescope for watching stars.
examples.chinese: 学校有一台用来观星的[光学]望远镜。

meanings.explanation: If you [make mistakes], you do something wrong or get the wrong answer.

examples.english: I sometimes [make mistakes] in my math homework.
examples.chinese: 我有时会在数学作业里[犯错]。

examples.english: Everyone [makes mistakes] when they learn a new language.
examples.chinese: 学新语言的时候，每个人都会[犯错]。

examples.english: It's okay to [make mistakes] when you speak English.
examples.chinese: 说英语的时候[犯错]没关系。

meanings.explanation: An [optical illusion] is a picture or a sight that tricks your eyes into seeing something that is not really there.

examples.english: The picture looks like it is moving, but it is just an [optical illusion].
examples.chinese: 这幅画看起来在动，但其实只是[视错觉]。

examples.english: The two lines look different in length, but that is an [optical illusion].
examples.chinese: 这两条线看起来长短不一样，但那是[视错觉]。

examples.english: The magician used an [optical illusion] to make the rabbit disappear.
examples.chinese: 魔术师用[视觉错觉]让兔子消失了。

meanings.explanation: If something happened [recently], it happened a short time ago, not long ago.

examples.english: I [recently] got a new puppy.
examples.chinese: 我[最近]养了一只新小狗。

examples.english: We [recently] moved to a new house.
examples.chinese: 我们[最近]搬了新家。

examples.english: She [recently] learned to ride a bike.
examples.chinese: 她[最近]学会了骑自行车。

common_collocations: play tricks on your little brother

meanings.explanation: If you [play tricks on] someone, you do something to fool them or make them believe something that is not true, usually as a joke.

examples.english: My brother loves to [play tricks on] me on April Fools' Day.
examples.chinese: 我哥哥最喜欢在愚人节[捉弄]我。

examples.english: Tom [played tricks on] his little sister and made her cry.
examples.chinese: 汤姆[捉弄]了他的妹妹，把她弄哭了。

examples.english: The funny clown [plays tricks on] the children and makes everyone laugh.
examples.chinese: 那个有趣的小丑[捉弄]孩子们，逗得大家都笑了。

common_collocations: realize that I made a mistake

meanings.explanation: If you [realize] something, you suddenly become aware of it or understand it.

examples.english: I [realized] that I left my umbrella at home.
examples.chinese: 我[发现]我把雨伞忘在家里了。

examples.english: She [realized] that the light was still on.
examples.chinese: 她[发现]灯还亮着。

examples.english: Now I [realize] why Mom always asks me to eat breakfast.
examples.chinese: 现在我[明白]妈妈为什么总让我吃早饭了。

meanings.explanation: [Sight] is the ability to see with your eyes.

examples.english: Birds have very good [sight].
examples.chinese: 鸟类的[视力]非常好。

examples.english: My grandma's [sight] is not so good, so she wears glasses.
examples.chinese: 我奶奶[视力]不太好，所以她戴眼镜。

examples.english: Reading in the dark is bad for your [sight].
examples.chinese: 在黑暗中看书对[视力]不好。

meanings.explanation: A [situation] is what is happening around you at a certain time and place.

examples.english: It was a difficult [situation] when the bus broke down on the way to school.
examples.chinese: 公交车在上学路上坏了，那是一个棘手的[情况]。

examples.english: Please tell me about the [situation] at home.
examples.chinese: 请跟我说说家里的[情况]。

examples.english: My mom always knows what to do in a bad [situation].
examples.chinese: 遇到糟糕的[情况]，妈妈总是知道该怎么办。

meanings.explanation: If something [seems] a particular way, it appears to be that way, although you may not be certain.

examples.english: The soup [seems] too hot, so I will wait.
examples.chinese: 这碗汤[好像]太烫了，所以我等一会儿。

examples.english: She [seemed] happy when she got her new bike.
examples.chinese: 她拿到新自行车时，[看起来]很开心。

examples.english: It [seems] like rain today.
examples.chinese: 今天[好像]要下雨了。

meanings.explanation: A [shadow] is the dark shape on the ground or wall that appears when something blocks the light.

examples.english: My dog makes a big [shadow] on the wall when the lamp is on.
examples.chinese: 灯亮着的时候，我的小狗在墙上留下了一个大大的[影子]。

examples.english: The children love to play with their [shadows] in the sun.
examples.chinese: 孩子们喜欢在阳光下和自己的[影子]一起玩。

examples.english: The tall tree cast a long [shadow] across the grass.
examples.chinese: 那棵高高的树在草地上投下了一道长长的[影子]。

meanings.explanation: [Pajamas] are soft, comfortable clothes that people wear for sleeping.

examples.english: I put on my [pajamas] before bed.
examples.chinese: 我睡觉前穿上[睡衣]。

examples.english: My [pajamas] have blue stars on them.
examples.chinese: 我的[睡衣]上印着蓝色的星星。

examples.english: The children wore [pajamas] when they stayed overnight at a friend's house.
examples.chinese: 孩子们在朋友家过夜时都穿着[睡衣]。

meanings.explanation: [Perhaps] is used to say that something is possibly true or possible, but you are not completely certain about it.

examples.english: [Perhaps] we can go to the park tomorrow if it doesn't rain.
examples.chinese: [也许]我们明天不下雨就能去公园。

examples.english: My mom said [perhaps] I can have a cookie after finishing my vegetables.
examples.chinese: 妈妈说我吃完青菜后[或许]能吃一块饼干。

examples.english: You should ask your grandma; [perhaps] she knows where your favorite storybook is.
examples.chinese: 你应该问问奶奶，[大概]她知道你最喜欢的故事书在哪儿。

common_collocations: otherwise we will miss the bus

meanings.explanation: You use [otherwise] to say what will happen if you do not do something.

examples.english: Hurry up, [otherwise] we will be late for school.
examples.chinese: 快点，[否则]我们上学要迟到了。

examples.english: Wear your raincoat, [otherwise] you will get wet.
examples.chinese: 穿上雨衣，[不然]你会淋湿的。

examples.english: Brush your teeth before bed, [otherwise] they may hurt.
examples.chinese: 睡前要刷牙，[要不然]牙齿会疼的。

meanings.explanation: If something [seems to] be a particular way, it looks or feels like it is that way based on what you see or notice.

examples.english: The black dog [seems to] like playing with me.
examples.chinese: 这只黑狗[好像]喜欢和我一起玩。

examples.english: My grandpa [seemed to] feel better this morning.
examples.chinese: 我爷爷今天早上[似乎]感觉好点了。

examples.english: This cake [seems to] taste like strawberry.
examples.chinese: 这个蛋糕[好像]是草莓味的。

meanings.explanation: If something happens [suddenly], it happens very quickly and when you do not expect it.

examples.english: The lights [suddenly] went out.
examples.chinese: 灯[突然]灭了。

examples.english: It started to rain [suddenly].
examples.chinese: 天[突然]下起雨来。

examples.english: The little dog [suddenly] ran away.
examples.chinese: 小狗[突然]跑开了。

meanings.explanation: Something that is [sticky] has a surface that things stick to, or it feels like it sticks to your fingers.

examples.english: My hands are [sticky] after eating the candy.
examples.chinese: 吃完糖后，我的手变得[黏黏的]。

examples.english: I used a piece of [sticky] tape to fix the torn page.
examples.chinese: 我用一块[黏的]胶带修好了撕破的那页。

examples.english: The honey on the table is very [sticky].
examples.chinese: 桌上的蜂蜜非常[黏]。

meanings.explanation: If you do something [straight away], you do it at once, without waiting or stopping to do anything else.

examples.english: When I got home, I did my homework [straight away].
examples.chinese: 我一到家就[马上]做作业。

examples.english: If you feel sick, tell your mom [straight away].
examples.chinese: 如果你不舒服，要[立刻]告诉妈妈。

examples.english: Dad called us for dinner, so we came [straight away].
examples.chinese: 爸爸叫我们吃饭，我们[马上]就过去了。

meanings.explanation: A [spike] is a thin, pointed piece of metal, wood, or other hard material that sticks out from a surface.

examples.english: The old garden fence has a sharp [spike] at the top.
examples.chinese: 旧花园围栏的顶部有一根锋利的[尖钉]。

examples.english: A tiny [spike] from the cactus stuck into my thumb.
examples.chinese: 仙人掌的一根小[刺]扎进了我的大拇指。

examples.english: The carpenter hammered a big iron [spike] into the gate post.
examples.chinese: 木匠把一根粗大的铁[长钉]钉进了门柱。

meanings.explanation: If something [snaps], it breaks suddenly with a sharp sound.

examples.english: The dry branch [snapped] in half.
examples.chinese: 那根干树枝啪地[折断]了。

examples.english: She [snapped] the chocolate bar into two pieces.
examples.chinese: 她把巧克力条咔嚓一声[掰]成两半。

examples.english: The pencil [snapped] when I pressed too hard.
examples.chinese: 我用力过猛，铅笔咔的一声[断了]。

common_collocations: see sb as a role model

meanings.explanation: If you [see somebody as] something, you think of them in that way.

examples.english: I [see her as] my best friend.
examples.chinese: 我把她[看作]我最好的朋友。

examples.english: My mom [sees me as] a little kid.
examples.chinese: 妈妈把我[看作]一个小孩子。

examples.english: We [saw him as] the leader of our team.
examples.chinese: 我们把他[看作]我们队的队长。

meanings.explanation: A [temperate] climate or region has weather that is mild, not very hot or very cold.

examples.english: The island has a [temperate] climate, so winters are cool and summers are warm.
examples.chinese: 这个岛气候[温和]，所以冬天凉爽，夏天温暖。

examples.english: Our town has [temperate] weather in spring, with neither very hot nor very cold days.
examples.chinese: 我们这儿春天天气[宜人]，既不太热也不太冷。

examples.english: Many plants grow well in [temperate] regions because the weather is mild.
examples.chinese: 许多植物在[温带]地区长得很好，因为那里的天气很温和。

meanings.explanation: A [niche] is a special place or role where a person or an animal feels right at home and can do their best.

examples.english: Tom found his [niche] in the school choir and loves to sing.
examples.chinese: 汤姆在学校合唱团里找到了自己的[位置]，他非常喜欢唱歌。

examples.english: Every animal has its own [niche] in the forest where it lives and finds food.
examples.chinese: 森林里每种动物都有自己的[位置]，在那里生活和觅食。

examples.english: After trying many sports, Lily finally found her [niche], and that is swimming.
examples.chinese: 试过很多运动后，莉莉终于找到了自己的[位置]，那就是游泳。

meanings.explanation: If you [speed through] something, you do or finish it very quickly, often without giving it enough attention.

examples.english: I [speed through] my homework so I can play outside.
examples.chinese: 我[匆匆写完]作业，就可以出去玩了。

examples.english: Please do not [speed through] the story; read it slowly.
examples.chinese: 请不要[读得太快]，要慢慢读这个故事。

examples.english: Lily [sped through] her book and missed some funny parts.
examples.chinese: 莉莉[一口气读完]那本书，错过了几个有趣的情节。

common_collocations: change the way we see things
broaden the way we see things
the way we see the world

meanings.explanation: [The way we see things] is how we think about or understand the world around us.

examples.english: Reading books can change [the way we see things].
examples.chinese: 读书可以改变[我们看问题的方式]。

examples.english: [The way we see things] helps us understand our friends better.
examples.chinese: [我们看待事物的方式]能帮助我们更好地理解朋友。

examples.english: Growing up changes [the way we see things] about the world.
examples.chinese: 长大后，[我们看世界的方式]会发生改变。

derived_forms: up to + number (e.g., up to five)
up to + time (e.g., up to an hour)
up to + quantity (e.g., up to 20 kids)

meanings.explanation: You use [up to] before a number or amount to mean not more than that number or amount.

examples.english: You can play games [up to] one hour a day.
examples.chinese: 你每天[最多]可以玩一小时的游戏。

examples.english: The little bag can hold [up to] ten apples.
examples.chinese: 这个小袋子[最多]能装十个苹果。

examples.english: We have [up to] ten minutes before the bus comes.
examples.chinese: 公交车来之前，我们[最多]还有十分钟。

meanings.explanation: A [trick] is a playful thing you do to make someone look silly or to make people laugh.

examples.english: My little sister played a [trick] on me and hid my shoes.
examples.chinese: 我的妹妹对我搞了个[恶作剧]，把我的鞋子藏了起来。

examples.english: It was just a [trick], so please don't be angry.
examples.chinese: 这只是个[恶作剧]，你别生气啦。

examples.english: The children played [tricks] on each other at the party.
examples.chinese: 孩子们在聚会上互相搞[恶作剧]。

common_collocations: tell the difference between right and wrong
tell the difference between two pictures

meanings.explanation: If you [tell the difference between two things], you can see or notice how they are different from each other.

examples.english: Can you [tell the difference between a frog and a toad]?
examples.chinese: 你能[分清]青蛙和癞蛤蟆吗？

examples.english: It's hard to [tell the difference between real flowers and plastic ones].
examples.chinese: 真花和假花很难[分辨]出来。

examples.english: My little brother can't [tell the difference between right and wrong] yet.
examples.chinese: 我弟弟还[分不清]对错。

meanings.explanation: If something is [useful], it helps you do things or it can be used for a good purpose.

examples.english: This small bag is very [useful] for school.
examples.chinese: 这个小包上学时很[有用]。

examples.english: I have a book about animals, and it is very [useful].
examples.chinese: 我有一本关于动物的书，非常[有用]。

examples.english: My phone is [useful] for taking pictures.
examples.chinese: 我的手机用来拍照很[有用]。

derived_forms: the result from using (prepositional pattern variant)
the results from using (plural prepositional variant)
common_collocations: the result of using a new tool
the result of using too much sugar
the result of using the right method

meanings.explanation: [The result of using] something is the outcome or effect that you get after using that thing.

examples.english: We can see [the result of using] sunblock when we don't get sunburned.
examples.chinese: 我们没被晒伤，就能看出用防晒霜的[效果]。

examples.english: [The result of using] too much sugar is a very sweet cake.
examples.chinese: 用太多糖的[结果]就是蛋糕特别甜。

examples.english: [The result of using] my new crayons is a very colorful picture.
examples.chinese: 用新蜡笔画画的[结果]就是一张色彩丰富的画。
